target.title: feat: clarify iOS Location Always permission flow
target.body:
Related: #99229
Related: #86217
Related closed candidate: #99235

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where iOS users could select Location Always in OpenClaw without the app clearly explaining whether iOS had actually granted background-capable location access. That made wake-up/location workflows ambiguous, especially when iOS only allowed While Using, denied access, or global Location Services were disabled.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds an explicit iOS permission summary for Location settings that separates the user's selected OpenClaw mode from the effective iOS authorization state. It also wires the background-location contract into the native configuration and location service path: background updates are only enabled for Always-capable use, and significant-change monitoring is stopped when the mode is disabled, downgraded, or no longer authorized Always.

This follows the current SettingsProTab pattern for now because #99231 may reshape the Settings UI.

#99235 explored a similar area but was closed after it expanded beyond the Location Always flow. This PR keeps the scope narrower: Location permission copy, native i18n inventory, Info.plist background location declaration, background/significant-change monitoring gates, and focused tests.

## User Impact

Users get clearer feedback when Location Always is selected but iOS has not granted background-capable permission. Operators and reviewers also get a cleaner contract for when the iOS app may use background location behavior.

Use cases covered:

- Keep OpenClaw reachable for location-triggered/background wake-up workflows when the user explicitly selects Always and iOS grants Always.
- Show a warning when Always is selected but iOS only grants While Using, so users understand background location will not work.
- Preserve the selected Always mode in that mismatch state instead of reverting to the previous app setting.
- Show a warning when location is denied, restricted, or globally disabled in iOS settings.
- Stop background/significant-change monitoring when the user turns Location off or downgrades away from Always.
- Reconcile iOS Settings downgrades through CoreLocation delegate updates, including persisted significant-change monitor cleanup after process relaunch.

## Evidence

- Rebased on current `upstream/main` before the latest push.
- Current head: `80d59fae9e814cfeecda225655dcd3db7fc84be3`.
- Redacted terminal proof artifact with explicit rank-up coverage mapping: https://github.com/PollyBot13/openclaw/blob/proof/pr-99247-location-always/proof/pr-99247/README.md
- iPhone life-test runbook for physical proof: https://github.com/PollyBot13/openclaw/blob/proof/pr-99247-location-always/proof/pr-99247/life-test-runbook.md
- `pnpm native:i18n:check` passed (`entries=2395 changed=false`).
- Targeted SwiftFormat lint passed for `SettingsProTabActions.swift`, `NodeAppModel.swift`, and `LocationPermissionSummaryTests.swift`.
- Targeted SwiftLint passed for `LocationPermissionSummaryTests.swift`. Whole-file `NodeAppModel.swift` lint still trips the existing cyclomatic-complexity warning outside this patch.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- Focused simulator tests passed: `OpenClawTests/LocationPermissionSummaryTests` on iPhone 17 / iOS 26.5, 10 tests, covering Always/While Using mismatch, denied/global-disabled state, downgrade cleanup, and significant-location monitoring eligibility.
- Built simulator app Info.plist includes `UIBackgroundModes = [audio, location, remote-notification]`.
- Fixed and proof-built the iOS Always prompt no-callback path reported during device prep: choosing Only While Using now completes the request, stops the Location row spinner, keeps Always selected with the mismatch warning, and leaves the picker usable.
- Installed proof build on Polly's iPhone: bundle `ai.openclawfoundation.app.test.pollybot-5y97h9j837`, version/build `2026.6.11 / 379`, built from head `80d59fae9` with local proof-signing entitlements stripped for the personal Apple team.
- Removed stale `locationLabel` helper that Periphery flagged after the effective-status row replaced it.
- Local Codex review after the latest ClawSweeper fix found no actionable regressions in the location permission summary, background monitoring controls, or Settings UI changes.
